iconic_games_note: As of the snapshot (2026-06-23), Lumen Field's first-ever men's World Cup matches have been PLAYED and are recorded above as historic results: Belgium 1-1 Egypt (Group G, 15 Jun 2026) and USA 2-0 Australia (Group D, 19 Jun 2026), both FIFA/ESPN-sourced. Four further 2026 matches at the venue (e.g. Qatar fixture 24 Jun, Egypt-Iran 26 Jun, a Round of 32 and a Round of 16) are upcoming/forward-looking and not asserted as results. Non-World-Cup context (clearly NOT World Cup matches): regular home of Seattle Sounders FC (MLS) since 2009, including MLS Cup matches; the Sounders set a club single-game attendance record of 69,314 at the Leagues Cup 2025 Final (3-0 win vs Inter Miami CF, 31 Aug 2025); the venue hosted 2025 FIFA Club World Cup matches; as an NFL venue it has hosted Seahawks playoff and NFC Championship games.

renovations.change: Temporary replacement of the stadium's artificial FieldTurf CORE with a stitched/hybrid natural-grass surface (natural grass woven with synthetic fibers) grown in Moses Lake, Washington; layers installed over the existing turf with new irrigation and vacuum ventilation. Grass used only for the World Cup. Turf-replacement work scheduled to begin after the Seahawks' 2025 NFL season ended in early 2026, targeted for completion by May 2026 (per KING5/Axios).

city_history.founded: Permanent non-Native settlement at Alki Point in 1851; the town was incorporated 14 January 1865, that charter voided in 1867, and Seattle re-incorporated 2 December 1869. Named for Duwamish/Suquamish leader Chief Si'ahl (Sealth).
city_history.significance: Largest city in Washington State and the Pacific Northwest, on Puget Sound. Known as the Emerald City; a major tech, aerospace (Boeing) and maritime hub. Lumen Field sits in the SoDo district just south of downtown.
city_history.football_culture: Seattle has one of the deepest soccer cultures in the United States. The Seattle Sounders FC (MLS, since 2009) routinely draw among the largest crowds in the league and are backed by highly-organized supporters' groups (Emerald City Supporters, Gorilla FC, Eastside Supporters, North End Faithful) often compared to European ultras; the city also hosts NWSL's Seattle Reign FC (at Lumen Field since 2022; rebranded back from OL Reign to Seattle Reign FC in Jan 2024). The Sounders sold out their inaugural MLS season and built an immediate season-ticket waitlist, and set a club single-game attendance record of 69,314 at the Leagues Cup 2025 Final (3-0 vs Inter Miami CF, 31 Aug 2025).

stadium_history_facts: Opened 28 July 2002 as Seahawks Stadium; built on the site of the demolished Kingdome at a total complex cost of about $430 million (~$770M in 2025 dollars per Wikipedia).

Renamed Qwest Field (2004), CenturyLink Field (2011), then Lumen Field (November 2020) after Lumen Technologies; for the 2026 World Cup, FIFA's corporate-name policy sets the sponsor name aside and the venue is branded 'Seattle Stadium'.
Owned by the Washington State Public Stadium Authority; designed by Ellerbe Becket in association with LMN Architects (and Streeter & Associates).
Home of the NFL's Seattle Seahawks since 2002, MLS's Seattle Sounders FC since 2009, and NWSL's Seattle Reign FC since 2022.
Standard configurations: ~68,740 for NFL (expandable to ~72,000 for special events), ~37,722 for MLS, ~10,000 for NWSL; club soccer attendance record of 69,314 (Leagues Cup 2025 Final, 31 Aug 2025).
Played on a 'FieldTurf CORE' artificial surface (installed March 2024) outside the World Cup; converted to a temporary natural/hybrid grass pitch (grown in Moses Lake, WA) for the 2026 tournament.
Located at 800 Occidental Avenue South in Seattle's SoDo neighborhood, just south of downtown.
